## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/label ``` The Usage and Disabled examples also use [Input](/components/input). Install it when copying those examples: ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input ``` To reproduce the styled checkboxes in the top preview, also install [Checkbox](/components/checkbox): ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/checkbox ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | label | `@components/cadence/label/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/label.json) | [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: label](https://cadence.dev/r/label.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. Label needs only the two files and packages listed above; no motion runtime, provider or additional item-specific CSS is required. Keep `label/index.tsx` and `lib/cn.ts` at the listed relative paths so the shared `cn` import resolves. Associate the label with a control using `htmlFor` and a matching `id`, or wrap the control as shown below. For Usage and Disabled, also copy [Input's source file](https://cadence.dev/r/input.json) to `@components/cadence/input/index.tsx` and install its additional package: ```package-manager npm install @base-ui/react ``` The top preview's styled checkboxes require [Checkbox's installation](/components/checkbox#installation) and its own dependencies and motion setup. Input and Checkbox are example dependencies, not dependencies of Label. The Wrapping example uses a native checkbox and needs no additional dependencies. ## Usage ```tsx "use client"; import { useId } from "react"; import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input"; import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label"; export function EmailField() { const id = useId(); return (
); } ``` ## Wrapping instead of `htmlFor` Either association works: `htmlFor` + `id`, or wrapping the control. Pick one per field and keep it consistent. This example wraps a native checkbox and needs no `id` or `htmlFor`. Clicking the words toggles that checkbox; it does not affect the separate checkbox above. ```tsx import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label"; export function WrappedPreference() { return ( ); } ``` ## Disabled The label follows the control without any prop: `peer-disabled:` handles a sibling control placed before the label; `group-data-[disabled=true]:` handles a disabled group. These two arrangements show both relationships. Set `disabled` on the actual control; styling a label never disables an input. `useId` keeps repeated fields independent. ```tsx "use client"; import { useId } from "react"; import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input"; import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label"; export function DisabledFields() { const id = useId(); return (
); } ``` ## When to use - Every input, textarea, select, checkbox, radio, switch, and slider that needs a visible name. - A group of controls that share one caption. - A field whose purpose is not obvious from the placeholder alone (which is almost every field). ## When not to use - As a placeholder. A placeholder disappears on the first keystroke and is not a name; use a real `Label`. - As a heading. If the text introduces a section, use a heading so it appears in the document outline. - For helper text or error text; those belong in the description/error slot so they can be wired through `aria-describedby`. ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------- | ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ | | `htmlFor` | `string` | – | Id of the control this label names. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. | All native `label` props are forwarded. ## Motion contract Authored intensity is **subtle**: Label declares no Cadence recipe; native content/layout and existing CSS state feedback remain unchanged. No motion (T0). A label is text; the only thing it reacts to is the disabled state, which is an opacity change on a token, not an animation. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - Renders a native `
